children: The Canadian dollar held near an earlier 19-month low against its US counterpart on Tuesday as investors assessed whether recent broad-based gains for the greenback had run their course and after Canada and China agreed to extend trade deals.
was trading 0.1% higher at 1.4290 per US dollar, or 69.98 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since April 2025 at 1.4315.

gave back some of its recent gains against a basket of major currencies. Data showing underlying strength in US retail sales reinforced economists' views that the Federal Reserve would continue raising interest rates after next month's widely expected hike.

"The greenback surged in the wake of last week’s hotter-than-expected October inflation report and hawkish guidance from Fed policymakers ... but now looks technically overextended against the euro, pound, Canadian dollar, and yen, suggesting that a period of consolidation could be in the offing," Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay, said in a note.
China will cut tariffs on more Canadian exports, including pork and seafood, Prime Minister Mark Carney's office said, as he hailed "greater predictability and stability" in relations with Beijing.
The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, was supported by continued tanker attacks and expectations of falling US crude stockpiles. US crude futures
were trading 0.9% higher at $86.47 a barrel.
Domestic data showed home sales and prices edged higher in October, but the moves were limited as the Bank of Canada began an interest rate hiking campaign.
Canadian government bond yields edged lower across the curve. The 10-year (CA10YT=RR) was down 1.1 basis points at 3.808%, trading toward the middle of its range in recent months.
